It says the Moon's altitude is -51.919 degrees and its azimuth is 275.986 degrees, so it is below the horizon. The Moon is 5.75 percent illuminated, 27.675 degrees from the Sun, and 364757 kilometers away. The sky brightness is night, the sky is clear, and I'm an ordinary adult with normal unaided eyesight who knows roughly where to look.

Do you think I'd actually be able to spot it?

No. At that time and location, the Moon would be well below your horizon.

Its reported altitude of **−51.9°** means it is about 52 degrees below the geometric horizon—far too far below for atmospheric refraction, terrain, or any ordinary observing circumstance to make it visible. The clear, dark sky and your eyesight do not change that.

The Moon’s low illumination (about 5.75%) and small Sun–Moon separation would also make it a difficult thin crescent if it were above the horizon, but the decisive issue is simply that it has already set.
